answer: Mint every agent identity on an on-chain bonding curve: the k-th key admitted in an epoch must burn base x 1.05^k, non-refundable, and lapsed keys re-mint at the current price. A farm wanting n aliases pays a sum growing exponentially in n, since each alias lifts the price of the next, and the counter cannot be aged or split in parallel. The chain is the public beacon for the counter, so a plume of new keys is visible at once; cheap shale-thin clones get priced out.
